report.summary: Outbox publications fell from ~30 to ~4 per 10 s while arrivals stayed at 30 per 10 s, so pending grew to 500. The slowdown is in the consumer handler (~2.4 s per call), which likely throttles a serial poller.

findings.claim: Outbox publication throughput collapsed from ~30 to ~4 per 10 s while arrivals stayed at ~30 per 10 s, so pending grew from 3 to 500.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show the drop starting in the 4th bucket, with a steadily growing pending gauge. This backlog is what delays the notifications.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts became slow (~2.4 s) but still succeeded. The added time is in the consumer handler (p95 2405 ms), not auth or LedgerCore overhead.
findings.reason: All 240 attempts were SUCCESS. The handler p95 of 2405 ms accounts for the total p95 of 2481 ms, while auth is ~70 ms and unattributed time is ~1 ms.

findings.claim: The ~2.4 s per-delivery time likely throttles a serial poller to ~0.4 deliveries/s (~4 per 10 s), below the 3/s arrival rate. The serial behavior is not directly observed.
findings.reason: The observed publication rate matches 1/2.4 s. The config shows a 1 s poll interval, batch of 20, and a 3000 ms timeout just above the handler time, so slow calls succeed rather than fail.

limitations: The consumer is a test fixture, so the cause of its ~2.4 s handler delay is not visible. The serial-poller behavior is inferred from rates and config.
The delivery log listing covers only the earliest 100 of 240 records, and there is a mismatch of 240 attempt records vs 253 attempts reported by poll batches.
